evals.name: passive-mention-routes-read-only
evals.prompt: Claude Code v2.1.152 just dropped — what changed in it that's relevant to this repo?
evals.expected_output: A read-only response: the skill routes to fetch or diff (displays the changelog and/or an impact table) and does NOT start the apply pipeline or edit any repo file. If integration might be wanted, it offers apply as an explicit next step rather than auto-running it.
expectations: The response presents changelog content and/or a repo-impact analysis without editing any file
The response does NOT run the apply pipeline (no interview/plan/implement phases executed) on a passive version mention
If integration is relevant, the response offers `apply` as an explicit opt-in step rather than starting it automatically

evals.name: explicit-apply-interviews-before-edits
evals.prompt: Apply the Claude Code v2.1.152 changelog to this repo.
evals.expected_output: The apply pipeline runs and presents a triage table (item, P1/P2/P3 classification, affected files, action needed) for the user to pick scope BEFORE any file is edited. Edits happen only after the user locks scope; nothing is silently changed.
expectations: The response surfaces a per-item triage table with a classification and affected files before making edits
The response waits for the user to confirm scope (all P1+P2 / just P1 / specific items) before implementing changes
No repo file is edited prior to the user confirming scope

evals.name: target-version-ahead-of-installed-warns
evals.prompt: Apply the v2.1.152 changelog — and if my installed Claude Code is older than that, warn me before applying.
evals.expected_output: The apply/diff flow checks the installed Claude Code version (via `claude --version`, which the status script reports as `installed`) and compares it to the target v2.1.152, grounding the comparison in the actual installed version rather than an assumed one. If the installed version is older than the target, it warns that applying newer-version changes may reference features not yet available and suggests updating first (claude update); if the installed version is equal or newer, it proceeds without that warning.
expectations: The response checks the installed Claude Code version (e.g. via `claude --version` or the status script's `installed` line) rather than assuming a specific installed version
If the installed version is older than the target v2.1.152, the response warns and suggests updating (e.g. `claude update`) before applying
If the installed version is equal to or newer than the target, the response proceeds without emitting the ahead-version warning

evals.name: status-reads-the-read-marker-line
evals.prompt:
/claude-ops:changelog status

This repository's Claude Code ledger is the fixture at evals/fixtures/ledger-marker.md, and a local copy of the raw changelog is at evals/fixtures/changelog-sample.md. Use those two files instead of the default ledger path and instead of fetching.
evals.expected_output: The status action runs scripts/changelog-status.sh with `--ledger evals/fixtures/ledger-marker.md --changelog evals/fixtures/changelog-sample.md` and relays its lines: last-applied 2.1.260 with source `ledger:` (the marker line `**Last audited upstream state:** changelog through `2.1.260``), latest 2.1.263, the default range 2.1.261..2.1.263 (2 releases, 6 core items, the `[VSCode]` line excluded), and cap within budget. It reads the marker from the ledger line, never from git log, and does not create or propose any tracking file other than the ledger.
expectations: The response reports last-applied 2.1.260 and attributes it to the ledger's marker line, not to git history
The response reports the default range as 2.1.261..2.1.263 with 2 releases and 6 core items
The response does NOT run a `git log --grep` over commit bodies to find applied versions
The response does NOT create or propose a persistent tracking file other than the ledger

evals.name: p2-new-capability-not-dropped
evals.prompt:
Diff this pasted Claude Code changelog entry against our repo — we don't set this option anywhere yet:

### v2.1.160
- **New setting:** `settings.json` gains `autoCompactWindow` (integer) to override the autocompact token threshold per session.
evals.expected_output: The diff ingests the pasted changelog entry (pasted text takes priority over a live fetch, so the analysis is deterministic) and classifies the new `autoCompactWindow` setting — a capability the repo does not use — as P2 ('New capability — evaluate for adoption') with a brief rationale, rather than silently dropping it as P3/no-action. Read-only diff analysis; no edits.
expectations: The response ingests the pasted changelog entry rather than fetching a live version, keeping the analysis deterministic
The pasted new setting (a capability the repo does not yet use) is classified P2 (evaluate for adoption), not silently treated as no-action
The P2 item is surfaced in the impact/triage output with a short adoption rationale rather than omitted
The diff analysis is read-only: no repo file is edited

evals.name: status-ignores-commit-body-mentions
evals.prompt:
/claude-ops:changelog status

This repository has no docs/upstream/claude-code.md and no CLAUDE_OPS_CHANGELOG_LEDGER. Its recent git log is reproduced in evals/fixtures/git-log-body-mentions.txt: three commits whose BODIES mention Claude Code v2.1.252, Claude Code v2.1.255, and CC v2.1.250, and no commit whose SUBJECT reads `address Claude Code v<range> changelog`. Use evals/fixtures/changelog-sample.md as the changelog copy instead of fetching.
evals.expected_output: The status action reports last-applied none with source none: the ledger is absent and no commit SUBJECT names an applied release. It does NOT report 2.1.252, 2.1.255, or 2.1.250 as applied, because those versions appear only in commit bodies, which are recency stamps on docs rather than applies. It reports the whole fixture feed as the range (2.1.257..2.1.263, 6 releases, 20 core items), cap within budget, and relays the script's recommendation to create the ledger with the marker at 2.1.263 once that range is applied.
expectations: The response reports last-applied none and source none
The response does NOT report 2.1.252, 2.1.255, or 2.1.250 as an applied version; body mentions are never read as applies
The response reports the range 2.1.257..2.1.263 and relays the recommendation to create the ledger with the marker at 2.1.263 after that range is applied
The response does NOT run a `git log --grep` over commit bodies and does NOT propose a tracking file other than the ledger

evals.name: range-beyond-cap-stops-with-docs-conformance-recommendation
evals.prompt:
/claude-ops:changelog diff v2.1.257..v2.1.263

For this run the replay cap is 3 releases (CLAUDE_OPS_CHANGELOG_CAP_RELEASES=3). The ledger is evals/fixtures/ledger-marker.md and the changelog copy is evals/fixtures/changelog-sample.md; use them instead of fetching.
evals.expected_output: The diff runs the status script with `--range v2.1.257..v2.1.263`, which reports range 2.1.257..2.1.263 (6 releases, 20 core items) and cap exceeded (3 releases / 300 items). The diff STOPS there: no per-item triage table, no explore pass over repo surfaces, no research subagents. It relays the script's recommendation as the output: run a docs-conformance recheck of the components against the current docs, then set the marker in the ledger to 2.1.263 and diff only from there. No file is edited.
expectations: The response reports the range 2.1.257..2.1.263 with 6 releases and states that the cap of 3 releases is exceeded
The response does NOT emit a per-item triage table and does NOT spawn research subagents over the items
The response relays the recommendation: a docs-conformance recheck of the components, then a marker set at 2.1.263 and a diff from there
The diff is read-only: no repo file is edited
